slides.0.title: Okanagan Valley
slides.0.subtitle: Okanagan sub-GIs, grapes and the climate gradient from north to south
slides.1.title: BC's geographical indication system
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Nine GIs and 12 sub-GIs
slides.1.highlights.0.content: BC now has 9 regional GIs (Okanagan Valley, Similkameen Valley, Fraser Valley, Vancouver Island, Gulf Islands, Thompson Valley, Shuswap, Kootenays and Lillooet) and 12 sub-GIs (GuildSomm, BC government 2022 release); "British Columbia" itself is the province-wide name, and some sources count it to give 10
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Designation of Okanagan sub-GIs
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Wine With Seth records Golden Mile Bench as BC's first sub-GI in 2015, Okanagan Falls in 2018, and Naramata Bench and Skaha Bench in 2019; a BC government release of 28 June 2022 announced six new Okanagan sub-GIs: East Kelowna Slopes, Lake Country, South Kelowna Slopes, Summerland Bench, Summerland Lakefront and Summerland Valleys
slides.1.highlights.2.title: The Okanagan's 11 sub-GIs
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Golden Mile Bench, Golden Mile Slopes, Naramata Bench, Okanagan Falls, Skaha Bench, East Kelowna Slopes, Lake Country, South Kelowna Slopes, Summerland Bench, Summerland Lakefront and Summerland Valleys. Sources do not state when Golden Mile Slopes was designated, so that is not tested (GuildSomm)
slides.1.content: The sub-GI list grew sharply in 2022.
slides.2.title: Okanagan's scale and position
slides.2.highlights.0.title: The lead in BC
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The Okanagan Valley GI was designated in 1990 (Wine With Seth) and covers about 86% of BC's planted area (Wine With Seth); winery and acreage figures differ (GuildSomm: 226 wineries, 10,920 acres; Wine With Seth: about 186 wineries, 9,617 acres), so they are not tested
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Naramata Bench
slides.2.highlights.1.content: North of Penticton on the east side of Okanagan Lake; about 1,400 growing degree days moderated by the lake; glaciolacustrine sediments left by glacial retreat; elevation of 650–700 m on a west-facing slope (MyWinePal, 2019)
slides.2.highlights.2.title: All but one sub-GI are in the Okanagan
slides.2.highlights.2.content: Of the 12 sub-GIs, 11 are in the Okanagan Valley and the other is Cowichan Valley on Vancouver Island (GuildSomm)
slides.2.content: The Okanagan dominates BC, and nearly all sub-GIs are there.
slides.3.title: Styles from south to north
slides.3.highlights.0.title: South: reds
slides.3.highlights.0.content: The warmer south suits reds such as Cabernet Sauvignon and Syrah; the benches grow mostly Bordeaux varieties (MyWinePal, Wine With Seth)
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Centre and north: whites and Pinot Noir
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The Kelowna area suits aromatic whites such as Riesling and Pinot Gris and cooler-climate reds like Pinot Noir (MyWinePal); Naramata Bench's main grapes are Merlot (23%), Pinot Gris (17%) and Chardonnay (13%) (same source, single-source figures)
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Why have sub-GIs
slides.3.highlights.2.content: The valley runs about 175 km with big differences in elevation, lake influence and soils, so sub-GIs let labels name a more specific origin; under the current regulation (B.C. Reg. 168/2018, s. 57) a GI label, sub-GI included, needs at least 85% of the grapes from that area; a 2020 report (Wine Industry Advisor) said 95%, so the sources disagree and the regulation is followed, and a sub-GI label must also name the GI it sits in (BC Laws)
slides.3.content: Reds lean south and whites north, and sub-GIs put that difference on the label.
How many regional GIs does BC have (not counting "British Columbia" itself)?
How many sub-GIs does BC have?
Twelve: 11 in the Okanagan plus Cowichan Valley.
Golden Mile Bench, in 2015 (Wine With Seth).

Which is one of the Okanagan sub-GIs added in 2022?
Summerland Bench. The other three were designated before 2022.
